updatedAt: 2026-08-01 — bounded review blockers fixed; full release verification green
subtitle: SQL query explainer & optimizer — CLI-first product build against PostgreSQL
headline: SQLSage installs as a built command-line product and supports catalog JSON, schema SQL, saved plans, reusable evidence bundles, and safe live PostgreSQL planning with explicit read-only EXPLAIN ANALYZE opt-in. M1–M7 run by default; all 12 corpus workflows and named correctness/intent gates pass. The one bounded product review is complete and its three release blockers are fixed.

events.msg: Postgres 16.14 started; shop schema created with baseline indexes only (PKs + two FK indexes).
Seeded 13.2M rows / 1.6 GB with deliberate skew: 85% complete orders, 92% bronze tier.
Corpus fixed at 12 queries, each carrying a distinct expert-known failure mode; 3 are correctness bugs, not slowness.
Ground truth captured: real EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, VERBOSE, SETTINGS) + median-of-3 timings, 6 ms to 6.8 s.
Corpus corrected by evidence: q10's textbook 'move filter out of HAVING' advice is WRONG on PG 16 — the planner already pushes it to a Bitmap Index Scan. Kept as a false-positive trap.
Wave A launched: M1 (IR) and M7 (report renderer) building in parallel.
Critic protocol fixed: each critic writes its OWN reference analysis from the real plan BEFORE reading our output, then diffs. Anchoring is the failure mode of review.
Verification harness built and proven: applies candidate indexes/rewrites in a rolled-back transaction, measures median-of-3, compares result digests.
Harness result on q01 — index ALONE is 1.04x SLOWER (date_trunc blocks it; still seq-scans, 650k rows filtered). Rewrite + covering index: 3.94x faster, Index Only Scan, identical digest.
SEED BUG 1 found and fixed: NULL rule (g%5) shared a factor with checkout rule (g%50), so every checkout was anonymous and q05's demonstration was meaningless. Moved to g%7.
SEED BUG 2 found and fixed: utm_source (g%4) shared a factor with event_type (g%10), so q12 returned ZERO rows. Moved to (g%7)%4. Now 111,589 rows / 20,000 customers.
Correctness bugs quantified on real data: q05 NOT IN returns 0 rows vs 196,000 for NOT EXISTS; q06 over-reports revenue by exactly 3.0000x.
Session limit reached. HANDOFF.md written with environment rebuild steps, verified reference numbers, blockers, and the round-2 plan.

Ground truth refreshed successfully: all 12 real plans captured with no errors; q11 remains the slowest at 7.0s and q10 remains a 10ms no-speedup trap.

Harness audit found that fingerprints were capped at 5,000 rows, risking false equivalence. Full-result multiset hashing now reports q07's true 149,000 rows; final artifacts will be regenerated after concurrent critic reads.
A second stale assumption was removed: PostgreSQL 16 does not have btree skip scan (introduced in PG18). q11's candidate index can avoid sorting but must still scan all index entries.

Blind M1 work found a catalog contract breach: PK/FK columns were brace strings, not string arrays. Introspection now casts name[] to text[]; the regenerated catalog validates all keys and relationships.
Clean ground truth complete: 12/12 plans, no errors or warnings, full row counts/digests (q07=149,000; q11=200,000), and validated catalog constraint arrays.

M7 builder complete: 11 focused tests + 4 report fixtures pass, including correctness-first ordering, incomplete inputs, rewrite/index coupling, and terminal parity. Blind critic still independent.

Cross-module decision: shared contracts now carry serializable nullability/subquery/group-expression metadata, Finding.category, and stable IndexRecommendation.id dependencies. Fresh Round-2 builders launched.

Round-2 builders complete: M1 passes 337 assertions (+69 adversarial); M7 passes 26 adversarial tests plus both-format dumps. Original critics are independently re-running their failures.

Post-interruption audit: M1 passes 373 assertions, M7 passes 32 tests plus dump checks, M5 blind reference is complete, database retains exactly 8 baseline indexes. Round-3 critic reviews remain pending.

Claude resumed from HANDOFF.md at the new standalone path. Re-ran both documented verification suites: M1 373 assertions pass, M7 32 tests + dump-report checks pass. Confirmed the live database still holds exactly its 8 baseline indexes.

Fresh independent Round-3 critics launched for M1 and M7, each instructed to treat builder-authored tests as claims rather than evidence and to reproduce the Round-2 counterexamples against live PostgreSQL before scoring.

Critics were also told to probe the NEIGHBOURHOOD of each prior failure — chained/multi-key USING, qualified forms, JSON round-trips, longer backtick runs, overflowing timing ratios — because a builder patching one reported case often leaves the family broken.
M6 blind reference commissioned in parallel: it must be written while no M6 implementation exists, which is the only moment it can be genuinely unbiased. All measurements rollback-safe.

M1 Round-3 critic: SCORE 60, NOT CONVINCED. Both Round-2 defects confirmed genuinely fixed and verified more broadly than before — USING namespace matches PG's own information_schema star expansion, 3VL null-rejection agrees 10/10 with the live server, JSON round-trip byte-identical, and a 22-case sargability battery found no false positives OR negatives.

But a NEW structural defect, untested by any prior round: fanOut is orientation-dependent. computeFanOut returns false as soon as the RIGHT side is unique, never asking about the left. I reproduced it — reordering q06's FROM items flips both joins to fanOut=false with the reason 'so this join cannot multiply rows'.

Verified on the live server that the reordered query is JUST AS WRONG: both spellings return 902,913,180 against a true 300,971,060 — exactly 3.0000x. So the correctness signal five downstream modules depend on vanishes based purely on how the author ordered their FROM clause. Confident-wrong: worse than silence.

M7 Round-3 critic: SCORE 75, NOT CONVINCED. All four Round-2 gaps verified fixed and the gates confirmed not over-firing; no special-casing (the critic proved the one 'shop' literal inert by renaming the schema throughout); q10 renders NO ACTION NEEDED in 55 lines with no speedup claim.

The M7 defect is editorial, not robustness — and it is the worst thing this module can do. I rendered it myself: 'Measured timing ... 3.94x speedup' sits directly above 'Do this first: 1. Create the index', when that index ALONE measures 113.3ms vs a 108.8ms baseline — 1.04x SLOWER and never used by the planner.

The 'index alone is slower' caveat lands at line 48 of 104 and the companion-index note at line 82. A reader who applies step 1 and stops ships a regression believing they got 3.94x — on well-formed input, with the coupling explicitly declared via requiresIndexes.

Round-4 builders dispatched for both modules with each critic's BIGGEST_GAP verbatim, plus an explicit do-not-regress list naming everything the critics verified as genuinely good. Neither module is complete; zero critics convinced.

All three Round-4 subagents terminated on an account-level session limit (resets 5:10pm ET). Integrity check: no partial edits — source mtimes unchanged, M1 still passed 373, DB still at 8 indexes. The M6 blind reference was lost after its measurements completed.
With subagents unavailable I did the M1 builder work directly. I am eligible as a builder because I have deliberately never opened a blind reference file; an independent critic can still review this.

Root cause: computeFanOut returned false the instant the RIGHT side proved unique and never asked about the left. Fixed by testing left-INPUT uniqueness (not one base table) and tracking multiplicity cumulatively across joins.

Contract change flagged, not made silently: JoinIR.fanOut now means 'multiplies EITHER input', plus additive optional fanOutSide and multipliedRelations. M7's 32 tests still pass, confirming the change is backward-compatible.

Verified: all three FROM orderings of q06 report multiplied={c,o} so sum(o.total_cents) is flagged every way it can be written; the same query WITHOUT order_items reports {c} and does not flag it. Orientation-independent without over-firing.

One existing assertion changed deliberately, not flipped to go green: q08's products join was asserted fanOut=false under the old orientation-dependent meaning. The server shows that join emits 19,935 rows over 250 distinct products — each product row repeats ~79.7x — so false was factually wrong.

393 assertions pass (20 new: three q06 orderings, mirror-image case, unique-on-both-sides, USING chain losing left uniqueness). M1 remains UNAPPROVED pending an independent critic — builder-green is not approval.
Session limit lifted. Relaunched all three outstanding items in parallel rather than serially: M1 Round-4 critic, M7 Round-4 builder, M6 blind reference.

The M1 critic is explicitly warned that the Round-4 fix was written by the orchestrator and self-verified — the exact arrangement this process exists to distrust — and told to treat NOTES.md claims and dump-ir assertions as an interested party's assertions, not evidence.

It is also pointed at the four axes I admitted NOT testing: FULL/RIGHT joins, LATERAL and derived tables, 4+ relation chains and self-joins, and whether the new noisiness is a sound contract or a burden that will produce false positives in M2/M4.

And told to independently verify the one assertion I changed (q08 products, ~79.7x) — 'was the assertion change justified by the server, or was a test bent to make a change pass?' That distinction is the difference between a fix and a cheat.

M6 reference redo now writes the file incrementally. The previous attempt reported 'all measurements complete... writing the reference' and then died, losing a full set of rollback-safe measurements for want of one file write.

Wired src/index.ts (pipeline) and src/cli.ts, with M2-M6 injectable as they land. All 12 corpus queries now run end to end without throwing. No integration path existed before, so contract mismatches between M1 and M7 were invisible.

The very first end-to-end run found a defect no module-level test could catch: with M2-M6 absent, q06 — revenue inflated exactly 3.0000x — renders 'NO ACTION NEEDED / No actionable problem was found in the complete analysis'.

Root cause is a CONTRACT gap, not an M7 bug: Analysis has no field expressing that an analysis is partial, so the renderer cannot know M2-M6 are missing. Absence of findings reads identically to a clean bill of health.
Deliberately did NOT edit src/types.ts to fix it — the M7 builder is mid-flight and editing the shared contract under it would conflict. Documented as a required change for the next round instead.

Interim mitigation: the CLI prints an unmissable incompleteness banner BEFORE the report, on stdout. Leading rather than trailing matters — a stderr note after the fact is lost the moment output is piped to a file.

Wrote eval/run.ts, fixing the documented-broken 'npm run eval'. It needs no database, so it is safe to run while a critic is taking timing measurements. 12/12 corpus queries compose cleanly through the full pipeline.

The eval harness independently confirms the fan-out fix end to end: q06 reports mult={c,o} and q08 mult={c,o,p} (correctly including products), while queries with no multiplying join report none. This is integration evidence, not a quality judgement — that verdict belongs to the critics.
Both previously-broken package scripts now work: npm run explain (src/cli.ts) and npm run eval (eval/run.ts). The handoff had flagged them as placeholders that fail.

All three R4 agents died: two 'Connection closed mid-response', one 600s stall. Six agents lost this session across three distinct failure modes. Database still clean at 8 indexes; no partial source edits.
The incremental-write instruction proved itself: M6's reference survived with 395 measured lines, where the identical failure previously destroyed everything. Now a standing rule in the handoff.

The M1 critic died before writing its critique — but its probe scripts survived and were re-runnable. Running them found THREE real defects in the fan-out fix I wrote by hand, none caught by my 393 assertions.

WORST DEFECT (fixed): multiplicity state was per-binder, not per-block. Two identical side-by-side derived tables produced DIFFERENT verdicts, and a CTE that multiplied c made an unrelated 1:1 join in main report a fan-out it does not have — a false positive, and the same context-dependence the fix was supposed to remove.

Fixed with block-scoped multiplicity (multipliedByBlock + currentMultiplied). Both cases now match their controls exactly. 3 regression assertions added, 396 total. Noting plainly: the earlier 393 passed while the bug was live, so that count was never coverage.

STILL OPEN: (a) old-style comma joins produce no JoinIR at all, so q06 written that way reports NO fan-out — the original orientation bug in a new disguise; (b) LATERAL reports multiplied=[c,t] when sum(t.total_cents) is actually correct, a false positive from ON true having no equi-key.

Honest status: M1 is further from done than it appeared. A hand-written, self-verified fix passed every test I had and was still wrong in three ways. Independent criticism found what my own testing structurally could not.
Session limit again (resets 11pm ET). Seven subagents lost this session across three failure modes: account limits, connection drops, and a stall.
